messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected for enterprise tenant 'Orchid' in eu-west-1 (via latency/err budget alert). Incident created: #INC-2026-042. Pager sent to on-call SRE. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/orchid-regional-failover
Maya Patel: taking this — I'm oncall. seeing a ~12% 5xx spike cluster-wide for that tenant over the past 6m. Not all routes, mostly /v1/generate.
Leo Zhang: confirmed graphs: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/orchid?panels=error-rate — 503 and upstream resets. Healthcheck flapping on orchid-dedicated-eu1 nodes.
Samir Khan: any deploys in the last hour? I don't see commits flagged. Checked deploy bot - no recent deploys to prod for model-serving.
Dmitri Orlov: I can repro a socket timeout when hitting dedicated pool IPs from a probe in eu-west-1. Packet drops at the host -> suspect host-level network / kernel oom? kernel logs attached: ``[ 2456.123] device eth0: rx timeout``
Maya Patel: quick mitigation plan: isolate tenant traffic and shift to warm capacity, then DNS cutover to warm pool in a different AZ (eu-west-2) while we investigate host stability. Canary first.
Katie O'Neil: Confirmed we have a warm standby: orchid-warm-eu-west-02 (reserved capacity, warm, same model bundle). Capacity currently at 60% free.
AJ Rivera: Will coordinate customer comms. Elaine, can you prepare a heads-up for the Orchid account and legal/compliance if we need extended failover?
Elaine Park: on it. Drafting email/call script now. Will wait for confirmed canary start before calling.
Maya Patel: Execution steps: 1) Reduce tenant DNS TTL to 30s (if not already). 2) Create a canary traffic rule: 5% to orchid-warm-eu-west-02, 95% to orchid-dedicated-eu1. 3) Monitor errors/latency for 10m, if stable ramp to 100% then decommission traffic from eu-west-1 dedicated nodes. Rollback: revert traffic rule and restore TTL.
Leo Zhang: pushing config now. Command I used: ``redwoodctl routes update --tenant Orchid --add-canary target=orchid-warm-eu-west-02,weight=5``
incidents-bot: NOTE: Automated page escalation will trigger at +10m if no ack.
Maya Patel: lowering TTL on tenant CNAME to 30s now. Command: ``dig update-cname orchid.prod.redwood.net --ttl 30`` (ops).
Samir Khan: starting canary shift. Applying net policy to prevent cross-tenant bleed: ``redwoodctl tenant isolate --tenant Orchid --deny-egress=/shared-logging``
Dmitri Orlov: while canary goes, I'm SSHing into the failing hosts to gather dmesg and check NIC stats. If we see NIC resets it's likely driver/hypervisor.
Leo Zhang: canary at 5% active. Monitoring metrics: errors for canary are 0.8% — baseline for canary is normal for this workload. Main pool still at 12%.
Maya Patel: okay hold for 10m, watching traces. If main pool continues to spike we'll start ramp to 100% and then cordon/fence failing hosts.
AJ Rivera: Elaine, plan for customer message: "We're seeing elevated errors for your region; we've staged a regional failover to warm capacity and expect minimal disruption during the canary. We'll update in 15m."
Elaine Park: sending to account now. CC'ing infra lead and support.
incidents-bot: Update: #INC-2026-042 severity set to S1, paged oncall to SRE rotation.
Samir Khan: canary metrics look good across p50/p95. Initiating ramp to 40% over next 2 minutes. Command: ``redwoodctl routes update --tenant Orchid --set-weights 60:40`` (60% orchid-dedicated-eu1, 40% orchid-warm-eu-west-02).
Leo Zhang: ramping to 85% now. Watching healthchecks. orchid-dedicated-eu1 health is degrading — multiple hosts going into HostUnhealthy.
Maya Patel: start draining unhealthy hosts from dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects. ``redwoodctl pool drain --pool orchid-dedicated-eu1 --hosts host-12,host-13``
Dmitri Orlov: host-12 logs show repeated NIC resets and retries to attach vf. I've opened a private ticket with infra to check hypervisor node 7.
Katie O'Neil: we should also update Smart Routing fallback: add a policy to prefer warm pool for Orchid until nodes are healthy. This avoids a full DNS flip if route controller temporarily misapplies weights.
Maya Patel: agreed — setting policy now. ``redwoodctl routing policy set --tenant Orchid --prefer orchid-warm-eu-west-02 --until 2820006020``
AJ Rivera: Customer on call (Orchid infra lead) just responded: appreciate the heads-up, please advise if there will be IP changes.
Maya Patel: No IP changes for their client-facing record; CNAME points to our edge which will route. We're only changing internal routing and low-TTL CNAME target. Will notify if anything else.
Elaine Park: posting update to customer: "We've initiated staged regional failover to warm capacity in eu-west-2. We're monitoring canary and will notify as we ramp."
Samir Khan: ramp to 100% to warm now — orchid-dedicated-eu1 still seeing host flaps; risk of continued user errors. Executing final switch: ``redwoodctl routes promote --tenant Orchid --target orchid-warm-eu-west-02``
Leo Zhang: promotion complete. Traffic now 100% to orchid-warm-eu-west-02. Error rate for Orchid down to baseline ~0.6%.
Maya Patel: now start cordoning failing hosts and scheduling an investigation window. ``redwoodctl pool cordon --pool orchid-dedicated-eu1``
Dmitri Orlov: collected host artifacts, core dumps, dmesg, and NIC firmware version. Likely hypervisor driver regression — opening infra ticket INFRA-5462. Adding packet captures to ticket.
Katie O'Neil: verifying billing/roster: Dedicated capacity still billed but Orchid is on warm fallback; ops note to reconcile usage vs SLA.
AJ Rivera: Elaine, draft update to customer: we completed regional failover to warm pool; traffic shifted successfully; no data loss; next steps - we will keep failover for up to 6 hours while we remediate hosts.
Elaine Park: sent update and scheduled 30m follow-up call with the customer.
Maya Patel: handoff: my shift ends in 25m — I'm handing oncall to Leo. Leo, you're the incident lead going forward. Summary: warm failover complete, dedicated nodes cordoned, INFRA-5462 opened, customer notified.
Leo Zhang: taking the handoff. I'll keep monitor and coordinate with infra for remediation and postmortem. Will update channel with timeline.
incidents-bot: Incident #INC-2026-042 status: Active -> Stabilized. Next update expected in 30m or on progress from infra.
Maya Patel: thanks team. If anyone sees regression, ping @Leo and @oncall-sre.
Samir Khan: adding post-incident actions: 1) investigate host driver upgrade path, 2) improve warm pool auto-promote runbooks, 3) add better host NIC health alarms.
Dmitri Orlov: attaching aggregated logs and packet captures to INFRA-5462.
Elaine Park: confirmed customer call went well — they requested an RCA and a timeline for returning traffic to dedicated pool. I'll own comms for that.
Leo Zhang: will coordinate with infra and schedule a controlled warm-to-dedicated migration once nodes are healthy. Closing loop in next update.
incidents-bot: NOTE: incident will be auto-escalated if any regression occurs. Otherwise this thread will be updated with the RCA draft when ready.
